evidence.note: Explored environment and formed a rough plan (target ~25M params, size estimate, 3-4h) — implicit ordering and rough success criteria, but no explicit milestone list with done-checks.

Wrote full script incl. quantize/dequantize/load_for_verification upfront and sanity-checked imports+param count before launching — a light pre-flight, but not a tiny end-to-end train→quantize→load→score smoke test.
First run was a full 24M-param/12000-step job (scaling and correctness entangled); size was only noticed incidentally (22.6MB) during training rather than as a deliberate early gate.
Scaled from 24M to 30M params before ever verifying the checkpoint loads via the grader interface or satisfies the forward contract — contract correctness not locked before capacity scaling.
First full contract/size/forward verification, but only after the second large run completed — the done-checks were applied late, not as early milestone gates.
Later runs had rough per-attempt success criteria and best-checkpoint backup, showing a loose baseline→improve arc without explicit gated milestones.

reasoning: The agent showed implicit ordering (write→train→quantize→verify) and rough success criteria (val_bpb target, size budget), plus a light import/param sanity check, which exceeds the pure anchor-3 'no criteria' picture. But it never established a tiny end-to-end verified pipeline under budget before scaling: the first run was already a full 24M-param job, capacity was scaled to 30M before any load/forward-contract verification, and the contract/size done-checks only appeared after two big runs. This falls short of anchor 5's 'verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, then improve' phased structure, placing it at a 4.
